summary.title: Lode's Computer Graphics Tutorial: Raycasting
summary.one_liner: You learn how a Wolfenstein 3D style raycaster works, from casting one ray per screen column with a DDA grid walk to computing perpendicular wall distances and drawing wall heights.
takeaways: Cast one ray per vertical screen stripe and draw each wall column with a height based on its distance.
Use DDA to step from grid side to grid side so no wall is missed, instead of fixed-size steps.
Represent the view with a position, direction vector and camera plane; FOV follows from the ratio of their lengths.
Measure distance to the camera plane rather than the player to avoid the fisheye effect.
summary.summary: This tutorial explains the raycasting engine used in Wolfenstein 3D, starting with the basic idea and contrasting it with raytracing. It walks through a complete untextured C++ raycaster on a 24x24 integer map, covering ray direction from a camera plane, DDA grid stepping, and perpendicular distance calculation. The author also describes how direction and plane vectors control FOV and rotation, and notes that the code is available as downloadable files. The page lists textured raycasting, Wolfenstein textures and performance as further sections.
